{{Quote|If you can bribe a member of Bespin's Wing Guard into taking you on a spin around Cloud City, you won't regret spending the credits. The views are stunning.|Excerpt from ''[[Ullok's Underground Guide to Bespin]]''|<ref name="NEGVV">''[[The New Essential Guide to Vehicles and Vessels]]''</ref>}}
'''Cloud City''' was an outpost and a [[Tibanna/Legends|tibanna gas]] [[Mining/Legends|mining]] colony above the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Bespin/Legends|Bespin]], named as such because it was perpetually surrounded by giant clouds. The city floated 60,000 [[Kilometer/Legends|kilometers]] above the core of the [[Gas giant/Legends|gas giant]]. It contained a large and famous luxury resort district on its upper levels, complete with [[Hotel/Legends|hotels]] and [[Casino/Legends|casinos]].

==Characteristics==
===Layout===
Cloud City consisted of 392 levels, in addition to level zero, a top-side surface-level plaza concourse. The level-arrangements were as follows:
*Level 1–50: The [[Tourist District]],<ref name="TJoY">''[[The Jewel of Yavin]]''</ref> consisting of luxury [[Hotel/Legends|hotels]] and [[Casino/Legends|casinos]] which made the city famous throughout parts of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]].
*Level 51–100: Upscale housing areas.
*Level 101–120: [[Administrative Levels|Administrative offices]].
*Level 121–160: Privately owned industrial areas with an infamous reputation, known as [[Port Town (Cloud City)/Legends|Port Town]].
*Level 161–220: General housing of the facility's workers.
*Level 221–280: [[Industrial Levels]].<ref name="TJoY" />
*Level 281–370: Gas refineries and [[Mining Quarter|miners' quarters]].
*Level 371–392: Contained the 36,000 [[Repulsorlift/Legends|repulsorlift]] engines and [[Tractor beam/Legends|tractor beam generators]] that kept the city afloat and in position.<ref name="EVV">''[[The Essential Guide to Vehicles and Vessels]]''</ref>

[[File:CloudCity_egvv.jpg|thumb|left|180px|Cloud City [[:Category:Technical drawing images|schematics]].]]
The main saucer-shaped city structure was 16.2 kilometers in diameter, and 17.3 kilometers tall. The city floated 60,000 [[Kilometer/Legends|kilometers]] above the core of the planet, which was an uninhabitable [[Gas giant/Legends|gas giant]].<ref name="EVV" /> Some of the nearby [[Tibanna gas platform]]s and other [[Bespin construction platform|industrial platforms]] were also considered part of the city.<ref name="SW:TFUn">[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed (novelization)|''The Force Unleashed'' novelization]]</ref> Six [[Gravity Control Generator]]s were placed on the upper level of the city to regulate the city's position. During the time of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] built the [[Bespin Government Center]] on the upper level.<ref name="SW:GB" /> The city's main function was to harvest [[Tibanna/Legends|tibanna]] gas, by using [[Tractor beam/Legends|tractor beams]] to draw the gas into internal refineries.<ref name="RS II guide">''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron II: Rogue Leader: The Official Nintendo Player's Guide]]''</ref>

===Government===
Cloud City was nominally controlled in all aspects by the [[Baron Administrator/Legends|Baron Administrator]], though the bureaucracy and administration was controlled by the city's business leaders, known as the [[Exex]], who did not consider themselves subordinate to the Baron Administrator. Furthermore, the [[Parliament of Guilds]] was a distinct faction which, by ancient custom, controlled the juries in all the city's courts.<ref name="The Illustrated Star Wars Universe">''[[The Illustrated Star Wars Universe]]''</ref> The [[Office of the Surgeon-General]] provided information to any and all major planetary systems for any travelers.<ref name="Star Wars Intergalactic Passport">''[[The Star Wars Intergalactic Passport]]''</ref>

===Population===
The last official census placed Cloud City's population at 5,427,080. That figure did not count the droids.<ref name="GG2" /> As Bespin's total population was estimated at 6 million,<ref name="EVV" /> the city was by far the dominant settlement on Bespin.

==History==
{{Quote|A Tibanna gas mine. Lando conned somebody out of it.|Han Solo|<ref name="ESB" />}}

===Early history===
Cloud City was first commissioned in [[1989 BBY]]<ref name="KotORCG" /> and built by [[Ecclessis Figg/Legends|Ecclessis Figg]], with the aid of [[Ugnaught/Legends|Ugnaught]] labor and contracted employees from the [[Incom Corporation/Legends|Incom Corporation]], around [[400 BBY/Legends|400 BBY]].<ref name="GG2" /><ref name="GATORW" /> The city's economy was centered on tibanna gas, which was crucial for the production of [[Blaster gas/Legends|weapons]] and [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrives]]. The unique atmospheric conditions of Bespin allowed for the natural production of spin-sealed tibanna gas, which was highly compressed at the atomic level and was an energy source for the most powerful blasters. The manufacture and distribution of this gas was tightly regulated. Since the initial construction of Cloud City, its official purpose was to mine for regular tibanna gas for use in hyperdrives, but secretly spin-sealed gas was also mined and exported for use in high powered blasters. Using the same canisters as the regular gas, the export of the spin-sealed gas was what allowed Cloud City to earn a self sustaining income.<ref name="Star Wars: Build the Millennium Falcon 3">[[Star Wars: Build the Millennium Falcon 3|''Star Wars: Build the Millennium Falcon'' 3]] - Guide to the Galaxy: Bespin's Settlements</ref>

[[File:Bespin_skyscrapers.png|thumb|right|250px|Some of Cloud City's high-rise buildings.]]
Under the leadership of [[Baron Administrator/Legends|Baron Administrator]] [[Ulumahal]] Cloud City transformed from illegal front to the jewel known in later years. During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the planet initially attempted to stay neutral. A Republic warship delivered dozens of orphans to an orphanage there, including a young [[Boba Fett]], who later [[Escape from Bespin|escaped]].<ref name="Crossfire">''[[Boba Fett: Crossfire]]''</ref> Despite Bespin's declaration of neutrality, the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] [[Battle of Bespin (Clone Wars)|launched an invasion]] of the planet, which was defended by at least one [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]], [[Glynn-Beti]].<ref name="Tethan Battle Adventures">''[[The Clone Wars: Decide Your Destiny: Tethan Battle Adventure]]''</ref> The planet, including its Tibanna gas colonies, fell to the Separatists initially.<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref><ref name="Star Wars: The Clone Wars video game">[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars (video game)|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' video game]]</ref> The planet eventually swung into the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic's]] hands after a series of orbital battles and [[Starfighter combat/Legends|dogfights]].<ref name="The Clone Wars Campaign Guide">''[[The Clone Wars Campaign Guide]]''</ref>

===Imperial era===
Months after the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Empire]] attempted to trade [[Nazren]] slaves to [[Darga Jiramma Mionne|Darga]] the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] in exchange for large shipments of tibanna gas during Cloud City's annual citywide [[Sabacc/Legends|sabacc]] tournament. The slaves [[Battle of Bespin (Imperial Period)|were freed]] by agents of [[Bail Prestor Organa/Legends|Bail Organa]] in [[Z-95 Headhunter/Legends|Z-95 Headhunters]].<ref name="wizards">{{DoD|The Queen of Air and Darkness}}</ref> In addition, Cloud City was also a major center for intergalactic travel, due to it being one of the spots designated within both versions of the ''[[Intergalactic Passport]]'',<ref name="Intergalactic Passport">[[Intergalactic Passport (real-life artifact)|Intergalactic Passport]]</ref> and one version in particular specifically stating that Cloud City provided refueling services and emergency repair facilities for anyone with the passport, as well as providing specific on all major planetary systems via the [[Office of the Surgeon-General]].<ref name="Star Wars Intergalactic Passport" />

[[File:Port_Town.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Cloud City's crime-ridden Port Town levels]]
Sometime during the [[Imperial Era/Legends|Imperial Era]], the office of Baron Administrator passed onto [[Dominic Raynor]], an unscrupulous business mogul from the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]]. While he proved to be a capable executive of the city's lifeblood mining industry, he was uninterested in governing and tended to assign city administrative posts based on cronyism and bribes.<ref name="TJoY" /> As corruption seeped into [[Bespin Wing Guard/Legends|Bespin's Wing Guard]] as well, organized crime began to flourish in the lower levels, most notoriously [[Port Town (Cloud City)/Legends|Port Town]] which housed most of Cloud City's landing bays and docking ports for [[Freighter/Legends|freighters]] and other commercial vessels. One such [[Landing Bay 124A|landing bay on level 124]] was effectively owned by crime boss [[Vorse Tabarith]] who had all of the responsible traffic control and customs officials on the take and could thus unimpededly smuggled in or out any cargo he pleased.<ref name="TJoY" /> [[Wonn Ionstrike/Legends|Wonn Ionstrike]], whose [[Lenushaa gang|gang of smugglers]] operated out of Cloud City along the [[Corellian Trade Spine/Legends|Corellian Trade Spine]], routinely shook down vendors near [[Market Row]], such as [[Danta Belissa's store]].<ref name="GG3-2">[[Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back (Second Edition)|''Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back'', Second Edition]]</ref> A similar protection racket, possibly on an even larger scale, was ran by a [[Lutrillian/Legends|Lutrillian]] named [[Sawthawne]], who was purportedly known as the "boss of Port Town".<ref name="GATORW" />

The debilitated [[Bespin Wing Guard/Legends|Wing Guard]] was rarely seen in Port Town, so long as criminals kept their malfeasance to the lower levels.<ref name="TJoY" /> But in [[2 BBY/Legends|2 BBY]], a group of mercenaries under the command of a [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] named [[Chop'aa Notimo]] attempted to overrun Cloud City's affluent upper levels and clashed with security forces. In the apparent absence of Baron Administrator Raynor, visiting [[Corellia/Legends|Corellian]] [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Garm Bel Iblis/Legends|Garm Bel Iblis]] took it upon himself to negotiate with Chop'aa on the City's behalf, but was taken captive by one of Chop'aa's henchmen, [[Kleef]]. Amidst the skirmish, [[Galen Marek]] arrived on Cloud City seeking to contact Bel Iblis on behest of [[Rahm Kota/Legends|Rahm Kota]]. After being informed by the city's chief administrator [[Lobot/Legends|Lobot]] about Bel Iblis' whereabouts, Marek [[Rescue of Garm Bel Iblis|took on the mercenaries]] and finally eliminated both Kleef and Chop'aa, thereby staving off the incursion.<ref name="TFUwii">''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed]]'' on [[Wikipedia:Wii|Wii]]</ref>

Only a few months earlier, Cloud City's glamourous [[Yarith Bespin/Legends|Yarith Bespin]] hosted a consequential [[Cloud City Sabacc Tournament|sabacc tournament]] that saw [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] walk away as the new owner of the [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']]. In the shadow of this event, representatives of several resistance groups clandestinely held exploratory but ultimately inconclusive talks about the formation of an [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance]].<ref name="RD">''[[Rebel Dawn]]''</ref> Among the participants were [[Bria Tharen]] and [[Winter Celchu]], the latter of which soon thereafter convinced [[Bail Prestor Organa/Legends|Bail Organa]] to join forces with Bel Iblis' [[Corellian Resistance/Legends|Corellian Resistance]], culminating in the [[Corellian Treaty]] of 2 BBY.<ref name="RD" />

===Administratorship of Lando Calrissian===
[[File:BobaFett-TrevasCV.jpg|thumb|right|180px|Boba Fett overlooks Platform 327]]
A year after the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], Cloud City was run by Baron Administrator [[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]], who had won administration of the city from Baron Administrator [[Dominic Raynor]] in a [[Sabacc/Legends|Sabacc]] tournament. Not much later Raynor hired the bounty hunter Bossk to get revenge on Calrissian. Bossk and his group of mercenaries [[Ambush in Cloud City|ambushed]] the new administrator in one Maintenance Level, but were unsuccessful.<ref name="Sore Loser's Revenge">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=swminis/article/soreloser|text=Sore Loser's Revenge|int=Sore Loser's Revenge}}</ref> During this period, Calrissian developed a tourism and casino industry.<ref name="BFI guide">[[Star Wars Battlefront: Prima Official Game Guide|''Star Wars Battlefront'': Prima Official Game Guide]]</ref>

During that time, Cloud City was almost subverted by an experiment. The droid [[X0-X1]] was designed as a systems planner, and designed [[Evolution Droid]]s to convert the city's population into droids. The experiment was thwarted by [[Walex Blissex/Legends|Walex Blissex]] and a team of Rebel agents.<ref name="Crisis">[[Crisis on Cloud City (adventure book)|''Crisis on Cloud City'']]</ref>

In the wake of the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]] in [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]], [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] and [[Princess/Legends|Princess]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] arrived in Cloud City, seeking refuge and repairs for their hyperdrive, with Solo confident that Calrissian would provide assistance. Unknown to Solo, Calrissian made a deal with the Imperial leader [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] to ensure the colony's continued economic autonomy. He promised to aid the Empire in taking his old friend prisoner, in order to lure the Rebel commander [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] to the city in a rescue effort.<ref name="ESB" />

[[File:EscapefromCloudCity-Leia.png|thumb|left|250px|Leia Organa fires at stormtroopers during the escape from Imperial occupation.]]
When it was clear Vader did not intend to keep his end of the bargain, Calrissian betrayed him and ordered his citizens to flee. However, Solo ended up being frozen in [[Carbonite/Legends|carbonite]] and taken away by the [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]]. Calrissian escaped with [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] and [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]] in the ''Millennium Falcon'', while Skywalker and Vader dueled in the depths of the city, with [[Duel on Cloud City/Legends|fateful consequences for the galaxy]].<ref name="ESB" />

===Imperial takeover===
After the escape of the ''Millennium Falcon,'' the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] and the Bespin security forces, including [[Lando's Commandos]], attempted to defend the city against the Imperial strike force sent to [[Occupation of Bespin|take control]] of it. The strike force landed on the city and established a beachhead. The Rebels attempted to disable the Gravity Control Generators to disable the city and prevent its takeover, but the Imperial strike force captured the generators, saving the city. The Imperials also destroyed the Bespin Government Center and built an [[Imperial Palace (Monument)|Imperial Palace]] in its place, cementing their occupation.<ref name="SW:GB" />

[[File:C_C_celebration.png|thumb|right|250px|Residents celebrate the Rebel victory at the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]].]]
During the occupation the Imperial forces present on Bespin were [[Battle of Bespin (Galactic Civil War)|attacked]] by a Rebel force.<ref name="SW:BF">''[[Star Wars: Battlefront]]''</ref> The Rebel's [[Rogue Squadron/Legends|Rogue Squadron]] also led a [[Raid on Bespin|raid]] in order to secure tibanna gas for the [[Alliance Fleet/Legends|Alliance Fleet]]. The Rogues destroyed three main power generators in the city to disable the Imperial defenses.<ref name="RS II">''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron II: Rogue Leader]]''</ref> Cloud City was [[Liberation of Bespin|liberated]] following the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]] thanks to the intel provided by Tian Chyler, a defector from the [[Imperial Security Bureau/Legends|Imperial Security Bureau]].<ref name="ChlyerDB">{{DB|character|chyler|Chyler, Tian}}</ref><ref name="WillrowHoodDB">{{DB|character|willrowhood|Hood, Willrow}}</ref>

===New Republic era and later history===
Around [[5 ABY/Legends|5 ABY]], [[Zorba Desilijic Tiure]] came to Cloud City in an attempt to reclaim the [[Holiday Towers Hotel and Casino|Holiday Towers]] Hotel and Casino which supposedly belonged to his son, [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba]] the Hutt, according to a will left by him. Whilst there using marked playing cards, Zorba became the new governor of Cloud City after winning it in a game of [[Sabacc/Legends|Sabacc]] against Lando Calrissian. When the [[Grand Hutt Council/Legends|Hutt Ruling Council]] declared Jabba's will to be a forgery, however, Zorba went into hiding.<ref name="Jedi Prince" />

After the rise of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], Cloud City rose out of obscurity and became a major exporter of tibanna gas for the Republic. However, Bespin lay relatively close to what remained of the Empire, and changed hands more than once over the subsequent decades. Cloud City had been reoccupied by the Empire by the time of [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Thrawn's]] [[Thrawn campaign|campaign]] in [[9 ABY/Legends|9 ABY]],<ref name="Atlas">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref>

[[File:Batbes1.jpg|thumb|left|200px|A [[Bespin Wing Guard/Legends|Bespin Wing Guard]] exchanging blaster fire with Baruk's thugs.]]
During the [[Empire Reborn]] crisis [[12 ABY/Legends|three years later]], the city's [[Industrial Levels|industrial levels]] were infiltrated by a mineral smuggling ring aided by [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]] garbage hauler [[Reelo Baruk]]. Lando Calrissian, who suspected [[Imperial Remnant/Legends|Imperials]] behind the unusually well-organized smuggling operation, travelled to Nar Shaddaa in hopes to persuade Baruk to reveal his employers, but found himself in a prison cell in [[Reelo Baruk's hideout|Baruk's hideout]]. After being freed by [[Kyle Katarn]], the two joined forces and returned to Cloud City, where they helped the [[Bespin Wing Guard]] to destroy the token garrison and their sympathizers. The [[Battle of Bespin (Empire Reborn)|action on Cloud City]] was a turning point in the crisis, as Katarn learned from [[Tavion Axmis]] on her surrender that his [[Jan Ors|partner]] had not been killed by her, changing the nature of his personal quest and perhaps averting a falling out between the powerful Jedi and the New Republic.<ref name="SW:JKII:JO" />

By [[35 ABY/Legends|35 ABY]], during the [[Dark Nest Crisis]], Bespin was troubled by the appearance of [[Tibanna tapper]]s, siphoning gas from floating refineries such as [[BesGas Three]] to sell elsewhere. Because of this, Cloud City's profits dropped by at least ten percent. Fortunately, the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] made an effort to stop the tibanna tappers.<ref name="DNII:TUQ">''[[Dark Nest II: The Unseen Queen]]''</ref>

[[Darth Krayt's Galactic Empire]] restricted the sale of tibanna to non-government entities, which resulted in many smaller operations moving out of Cloud City. As a result, it became a darker and more dangerous place. The Baron administrator [[Ormo Haddon]] had moved the business and entertaining areas to the central locations of the city, leaving the outskirts abandoned and completely lawless.<ref name="LECG" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:MCQ-cloudcity.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Concept art by [[Ralph McQuarrie]].]]
In the [[1974]] [[The Star Wars rough draft|rough draft]] of ''A New Hope'', a city on [[Alderaan (The Star Wars)|Alderaan]], which is set as a giant gas planet and the capital of the [[Galactic Empire (The Star Wars)|New Galactic Empire]] at that time, resembles the Cloud City of [[Bespin/Legends|Bespin]] in [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''Star Wars'': Episode V ''The Empire Strikes Back'']], released in [[1980]]. When [[Ralph McQuarrie]] began conceptual work for the [[Adventures of the Starkiller, Episode I: The Star Wars|second draft]], he designed the [[Imperial City of Alderaan]]. The art he provided was the inspiration for the look of Cloud City, differing only in minor respects from the city as seen in ''The Empire Strikes Back''.

The [[2001]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]'' offers players the chance to play the Occupation of Bespin on Cloud City during the Darth Vader campaign. The campaign is also included in the game's [[2001]] expansion pack [[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds: Clone Campaigns|''Clone Campaigns'']]. Cloud City also appears in two separate battles in the [[2004]] video game, ''[[Star Wars: Battlefront]]'', although [[Leland Chee]], the [[Lucasfilm]] manager of the [[Holocron continuity database]], has stated the game's storyline's is [[Canon|s-canon]], or of secondary continuity.<ref name="Blog">{{Blog|holocron|56|starwars.com forum HolocronKeeper comments archive}}</ref>

The sky above Cloud City serves as a location for a Versus Mode match in ''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron III: Rebel Strike]]''.
